mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to the prior month signals monetary easing, which reduces discount rates for equity cash flows and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% indicates a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.0%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 and housing starts (HOUST) above 1100 thousand units signals robust manufacturing and construction activity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 100 and HOUST > 1100, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL year-over-year change > 3.0%), a decline in the year-over-year CPI change signals reduced inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL year-over-year change > 3.0% and the change subsequently declines, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand for residential construction, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to short-term economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2.0%, it indicates robust economic expansion that typically produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 2.0%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market strength that fuels consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), a decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs fall.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and then declines, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.
